title: Spengler leads a BMW 1-2-3 at the Red Bull Ring
dek: Bruno Spengler converted pole into victory at the Red Bull Ring, heading a BMW 1-2-3 ahead of rookies Marco Wittmann and Timo Glock and taking the championship lead from Mike Rockenfeller.

chapters.title: A tight title fight reaches Austria
text: The 2013 DTM reached the Red Bull Ring for the third of its ten races with the top of the table tightly packed. Mike Rockenfeller led the drivers' standings on 29 points after winning at Brands Hatch for Phoenix Racing, one point ahead of reigning champion Bruno Spengler on 28, with Augusto Farfus, the winner of the Hockenheim opener, third on 25.

Spielberg also brought a first look at how the newcomers would handle a fast, flowing track. BMW Team MTEK, a new squad for 2013, ran two rookies in Marco Wittmann and Timo Glock, and this was only the third DTM start for each. Robert Wickens came off a podium at Brands Hatch, and Martin Tomczyk was looking to recover after a rival car spoiled his race in Kent.

The tyre question loomed as large as pace. Hankook supplied a standard compound and a quicker but shorter-lived option, and with DRS in play for any car within range of the one ahead, the order of the stints was expected to matter as much as outright speed.

chapters.title: Spengler beats Wittmann by 0.111s
text: BMW looked the quickest of the three manufacturers from the start of the four-part qualifying session, and Spengler and Wittmann traded the fastest times throughout. Spengler took pole for the BMW Team Schnitzer car with 1:24.836 after being behind the rookie at the second sector, with Wittmann 0.111 seconds adrift on 1:24.947 to put the new MTEK team on the front row.

Mortara was the best of the Audis in third on 1:25.036, ahead of Farfus in the RBM BMW on 1:25.183. Timo Scheider, Filipe Albuquerque and Wickens set 1:24.887, 1:24.922 and 1:24.973 in the third session for fifth, sixth and seventh, Wickens leading the Mercedes drivers.

Rockenfeller qualified eighth but was given a five-place grid penalty for failing to slow sufficiently under yellow flags in morning practice, which dropped him to 13th. Andy Priaulx, the slowest in the first session, took the same penalty and started last. Tomczyk and Gary Paffett each moved up a place to eighth and ninth, even though Paffett had no time in the third session after his Mercedes lost power on its out lap. Mattias Ekström was out in the second session and started 15th, Glock 12th and Christian Vietoris 16th.

chapters.title: Spengler escapes the DRS window
text: Spengler led away from pole and spent the first three laps pushing hard to get out of DRS range of Wittmann, because he expected to be heavily attacked. Mortara moved up to second at the start but was soon behind Wittmann again, and the field settled in behind a BMW-led front group.

Early skirmishes were rough. Paffett and Tomczyk touched at Turn 3 as the Mercedes passed the BMW, and Paffett was given a two-second stop penalty, and a few laps later Roberto Merhi's Mercedes made contact with the same BMW, earning the Spaniard a ten-second penalty. Tomczyk's car was damaged and he retired after 29 laps.

The first stops began early for those on the option compound. Glock and Rockenfeller both came in around lap four or five to switch from standard to option tyres, a gamble that sent them forward from 12th and 13th on the grid. Joey Hand's race ended early when a front-left wheel came loose after his first stop at RBM.

chapters.title: Glock's slow stop hands second to Wittmann
text: Glock's long option stint took him from 12th on the grid to within about a second of Spengler once the first round of stops was done, and for a time he looked an outside bet for the win. A delay fitting his front-left wheel at his second stop, on lap 33, cost him more than a second and dropped him behind Wittmann, who had run in the top three for most of the afternoon.

Spengler, who started on options, ran a long first stint and then took a late second stop on lap 41, six laps from the end. Spengler believed the call decisive: Wittmann had closed to within 0.8 seconds at one point.

Audi's best drives came from the back of the grid. Rockenfeller and Ekström both ran long final stints on the standard compound and carved through the field, with Rockenfeller passing Farfus and Dirk Werner among others. Mortara was the unlucky one: he and Wittmann made contact shortly after the BMW's last stop, damaging the Rosberg Audi and sending him from podium contention to the pits and ultimately 15th.

chapters.title: Spengler wins by 1.550s
text: Spengler took the flag after 47 laps in 1:08:35.249, 1.550 seconds ahead of Wittmann, who set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:25.505 on lap six. Glock was a further 4.954 seconds back in third, completing the first BMW 1-2-3 since the manufacturer returned to the series in 2012 and giving the new MTEK team its first podium finishes.

Rockenfeller was fourth, 9.183 seconds behind the winner and just 2.679 seconds short of the podium, having started 13th. Ekström completed his climb from 15th to fifth with a pass on Farfus in the closing laps that left bodywork flying from his car. Farfus held sixth for RBM.

Vietoris was seventh and the best of the Mercedes, ahead of Werner, who took eighth for Schnitzer, Paffett in ninth and Pascal Wehrlein in tenth. Wickens, seventh on the grid, could do no better than 12th.

chapters.title: Spengler takes the championship lead
text: Spengler called the 1-2-3 "simply sensational", but insisted the win had not been as easy as it looked: he had to push through the middle of his first stint to stay in front. He credited his engineer and the pit crew, while Schnitzer team principal Charly Lamm said everything had come together, from the strategy to the stops. BMW Motorsport director Jens Marquardt called it a historic result and singled out the new MTEK team for a podium in only its third race.

The result moved Spengler to the top of the standings on 53 points, 12 clear of Rockenfeller, who dropped to second on 41. Farfus stayed third on 33, one point ahead of Wittmann, whose second place lifted him to 32, with Vietoris on 25 and Werner on 22 completing the top six. Glock said the option tyre suited him perfectly, and said he was relaxed about the races to come.

Audi left Austria with mixed feelings. Rockenfeller said fourth from 13th was a very good result, and that the car had been so good that he regretted the grid penalty, a penalty Audi's own release called controversial. Audi's head of DTM, Dieter Gass, said the team had expected more after a promising Saturday and had lost its three best-placed cars during the race, while Audi's motorsport chief Wolfgang Ullrich said he disagreed with some of the decisions of the race directors.

The other camps took their own lessons. Farfus said his RBM car was difficult to drive and that he was glad simply to bring points home, while Ekström summed up his weekend as a horrible Saturday followed by an amazing race. Mercedes had a disappointing day, with Vietoris's seventh the best result of its drivers. Wickens said his race went nowhere near to plan, though he said he had not been stuck in traffic and had made no mistakes. Attention now turns to the Lausitzring, where the series returns on 16 June.

facts.v: Bruno Spengler won over 47 laps in 1:08:35.249, with Marco Wittmann 1.550 seconds back and Timo Glock 6.504 behind in third.
